reply: Acme Cloud is a managed cloud infrastructure platform for small and mid-sized engineering teams. It combines compute, managed databases, object storage, and a built-in deployment pipeline in one dashboard, enabling teams to ship applications without hiring a dedicated DevOps engineer. Its core products include on-demand virtual machines and containers, managed PostgreSQL and MySQL databases, and S3-compatible object storage with CDN. (Source: Acme Cloud: Product Overview)

The Starter plan costs $49 per user per month. It includes up to 10 users, 5 data sources, 1 million events per month, ready-made dashboards, and email support with next business day response. It is designed for small teams replacing spreadsheet reporting. (Source: Acme Cloud — Product Guide, p. 3)

The Growth plan costs $99 per user per month and includes unlimited users, 25 data sources, 20 million events per month, AI insights and smart alerts, custom health scores, and priority support with a 4-hour response time. It is designed for scaling companies running revenue and product on data. There is a 14-day free trial requiring a credit card but no charge until the trial ends. (Source: Acme Cloud — Product Guide, Pricing and Plans)
The Starter plan includes up to 1 million events per month. (Source: acme-cloud-product-guide.pdf, p. 3)

Yes, Acme Cloud offers a 14-day free trial for the Starter and Growth plans. The Starter plan trial requires no credit card, while Growth and Scale plans ask for a card but do not charge until the trial ends. The trial converts to a paid subscription unless canceled before it ends (Source: Acme Cloud FAQ and Pricing and Plans).

Yes, there is a discount for paying yearly instead of monthly. Annual prepayment gives you 2 months free, effectively reducing the cost compared to monthly billing. You can select annual billing at checkout to apply this discount (Source: 02-acme-cloud-pricing-and-plans.pdf, p. 3).
Your data and questions are never used to train AI models shared across customers at Acme Cloud. (Source: acme-cloud-product-guide.pdf, p. 3-4)

Your data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit for all customer data. This ensures strong encryption both when data is stored and when it is being transmitted. (Source: Acme Cloud: Security, Compliance and Use Cases)

Yes, you can choose EU hosting when you sign up with Acme Cloud. For example, EU customers are served from the Frankfurt region to meet data residency expectations. This ensures your data is hosted within the EU (Source: Acme Cloud — Product Guide, p. 3; Acme Cloud: Security, Compliance and Use Cases, p. 1).

Acme Cloud connects natively to Salesforce and HubSpot as CRM integrations. These are part of the native connectors along with Stripe, Chargebee, Segment, Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, Zendesk, Intercom, and Slack (Source: acme-cloud-product-guide.pdf, p. 2).

SSO (SAML SSO) is included in the Scale plan. The Scale plan is recommended for teams with 15+ developers who need SSO, high availability, or a 99.99% SLA. (Source: 04-acme-cloud-onboarding-guide.pdf, p. 2)

Setup typically begins with deploying a staging environment, connecting the repository, and setting up alerts in the first week. The process includes migrating the database, running the app in parallel with the old provider, load-testing, tuning autoscaling, and enabling preview environments over the next few weeks. Production traffic is usually switched over by week four, with the old setup decommissioned after a stable operation period. Initial setup steps like issuing credentials happen automatically within about 10 minutes. (Source: Acme Cloud: Getting Started Guide)

Acme Cloud pricing is listed in USD only. Payment methods accepted include major credit and debit cards on all plans, and ACH or wire transfer for annual plans and Enterprise agreements. There is no mention of payment in Indian rupees specifically. (Source: Acme Cloud: Pricing and Plans)
The Growth plan includes 25 data sources. (Source: Acme Cloud — Product Guide, p. 3)

Acme Cloud is not currently HIPAA compliant and does not sign business associate agreements, so it is not suitable for workloads containing protected health information. HIPAA compliance is under evaluation with no committed date. (Source: Acme Cloud: Security, Compliance and Use Cases, p. 1 and 3)
Yes, Acme Cloud is ISO 27001 certified. (Source: 05-acme-cloud-security-and-use-cases.pdf, p. 1 and p. 3)

Yes, Acme Cloud posts uptime incidents to a public status page where you can see incidents. Customers are notified of security incidents affecting their data without undue delay and within 72 hours at the latest, and post-incident reports are shared with affected customers. (Source: Acme Cloud: Security, Compliance and Use Cases)
The sales team coordinates with the security team and typically returns completed security questionnaires within five business days. (Source: Acme Cloud: Frequently Asked Questions)

Your data can be stored in different regions, including the Frankfurt region in the EU to meet data residency expectations. The platform supports read replicas in the same or a different region, allowing flexibility in data storage locations (Source: Acme Cloud: Security, Compliance and Use Cases, p. 1; Acme Cloud: Product Overview, p. 2).

There are no setup fees and no cancellation fees. Monthly plans have no minimum commitments and can be changed or cancelled anytime. Annual plans are refundable within 30 days of purchase. (Source: Acme Cloud: Pricing and Plans, FAQ)

Acme Cloud has native connectors for several platforms including Stripe, Chargebee, Salesforce, HubSpot, Segment, Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, Zendesk, Intercom, and Slack. However, Zoho CRM is not listed among the native integrations. Product events can also be sent through SDKs or the REST events API. (Source: Acme Cloud — Product Guide)

Acme Cloud does not provide an on-premises version for installation on your own servers. The platform is hosted on top-tier data center providers with strong infrastructure and application security measures. On-premises or bare-metal hosting is listed as a poor fit for Acme Cloud. (Source: 05-acme-cloud-security-and-use-cases.pdf, p. 2; 03-acme-cloud-faq.pdf, p. 1)
